headline: Brazil's starting XI announced for Morocco clash
summary: Neymar remains on the bench as Brazil prepares to face Morocco with a surprise lineup.
details: Brazil has revealed its starting eleven for the upcoming match against Morocco, featuring several surprise selections in the lineup.
Star player Neymar will not be in the starting XI and will instead remain on the bench for the match.
The team's preparation has been marked by high expectations, with the Brazilian President even urging the squad to play with more 'heart'.
Fans in Bangladesh, particularly in Madarganj and Gaibandha, have shown immense excitement, with some performing prayers to end Brazil's trophy drought.

headline_marked: Stoppage-time goal: [[Qatar clinch first World Cup point]] in 1-1 draw with Switzerland
headline: Stoppage-time goal: Qatar clinch first World Cup point in 1-1 draw with Switzerland
summary: Captain Boualem Khoukhi scored a dramatic 94th-minute equalizer to rescue a point for the Gulf nation in San Francisco.
details: Qatar celebrated their first-ever World Cup point after a dramatic 1-1 draw against Switzerland. Captain Boualem Khoukhi secured the result with a stoppage-time header in the 94th minute.
Switzerland had dominated much of the match, recording 26 goal attempts compared to Qatar's seven. Breel Embolo had given the Swiss an early lead in the 17th minute via a penalty.
The penalty was awarded after Qatar goalkeeper Mahmoud Abunada clashed with Remo Freuler in the six-yard box, a decision confirmed after a lengthy VAR check.
Despite the Swiss pressure, Qatar remained resilient. The breakthrough came when Homam Ahmed delivered a precise cross for Khoukhi to thump home, sparking wild celebrations.
The match took place at the home of the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, with an official attendance of 67,966 fans.
The result leaves Group B wide open, with all teams currently locked on one point each following Canada's 1-1 draw with Bosnia & Herzegovina.
Qatar will next face co-hosts Canada in Vancouver, while Switzerland is scheduled to play Bosnia & Herzegovina in Los Angeles.
caption:
A 94th-minute header! Qatar secures their first-ever World Cup point in a stunning draw against Switzerland.

Qatar celebrated their first-ever World Cup point after a dramatic 1-1 draw against Switzerland. Captain Boualem Khoukhi secured the result with a stoppage-time header in the 94th minute.

Switzerland had dominated much of the match, recording 26 goal attempts compared to Qatar's seven. Breel Embolo had given the Swiss an early lead in the 17th minute via a penalty.

The penalty was awarded after Qatar goalkeeper Mahmoud Abunada clashed with Remo Freuler in the six-yard box, a decision confirmed after a lengthy VAR check.

Despite the Swiss pressure, Qatar remained resilient. The breakthrough came when Homam Ahmed delivered a precise cross for Khoukhi to thump home, sparking wild celebrations.

The match took place at the home of the NFL's San Francisco 49ers, with an official attendance of 67,966 fans.

The result leaves Group B wide open, with all teams currently locked on one point each following Canada's 1-1 draw with Bosnia & Herzegovina.

Qatar will next face co-hosts Canada in Vancouver, while Switzerland is scheduled to play Bosnia & Herzegovina in Los Angeles.
